learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the science of extending the shelf life of food, preventing spoilage, and how raw agriculture products are transformed into tasty, shelf-stable supermarket foods!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the set of methods and techniques used to transform raw ingredients into food, or to transform food into other forms for consumption by humans or animals at home or by the food processing industry.

Foods are classified by shelf life: Perishable (spoils in a few days, e.g., milk, meat), Semi-perishable (lasts weeks, e.g., potatoes, onions), and Non-perishable (lasts months/years, e.g., rice, dried beans).
Food spoilage is caused by microorganisms (bacteria, yeast, molds), natural food enzymes (which cause over-ripening), insects, and physical damage like bruising.

Preservation stops spoilage by manipulating the environment. Main principles are: Heat (boiling/canning to kill germs), Cold (freezing to slow growth), Dehydration (removing moisture germs need), and Preservatives (adding salt, sugar, or chemicals).

This means changing a raw agricultural product into something with a longer shelf life and higher market value. For example, changing cheap raw tomatoes into an expensive, long-lasting bottle of ketchup.

fun_activity.title: 🍎 The Apple Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Cut an apple into slices. Leave one slice on the counter, put one in the fridge, and coat one heavily in lemon juice (acid/preservative). Check back in 3 hours. Which one turned brown fastest? This shows how enzymes and preservation methods work!

exam_tips: 📌 Always cite the 3 classes of foods based on perishability (perishable, semi-perishable, non-perishable) with accurate examples.
📌 Know the definition of 'Pasteurization' (heating at a specific temperature to kill harmful bacteria, commonly used for milk).
📌 Value addition is a key concept—be prepared to explain how processing benefits both the farmer (profit) and consumer (convenience).
quick_recap: ⭐ Food technology combines food science, engineering, and culinary arts.
⭐ Removing moisture (drying) or reducing temperature (freezing) prevents microorganisms from multiplying.
⭐ Processed foods save time, ensure food safety, and allow us to eat seasonal fruits and vegetables all year round.
